title: Differentially Private Two-Stage Gradient Descent for Instrumental Variable Regression
claim: A valid instrument affects the outcome only through the endogenous regressor, which lets us handle hidden confounding that biases direct estimation.
layout: Single causal diagram, left-to-right chain with confounder below, dashed red excluded path
description: A single causal DAG with three nodes in a row. An ellipse labeled 'Instrument z' sits at left, a rounded box 'Endogenous regressor x' in the middle, and a rounded box 'Outcome y' at right. Solid blue arrows run z→x, labeled 'relevance', and x→y, labeled 'causal effect'. A red dashed arc runs over the top from z to y. It is crossed out with a bold red X and titled 'Exclusion: No direct z→y path'. At the bottom right, a gray dashed ellipse 'Unobserved confounder u' sends black dashed arrows up to both x and y. The eye goes first to the red crossed-out arc, then follows the blue chain left to right. Colors separate allowed paths (blue), forbidden path (red), and hidden confounding (gray and black dashed).
caption: IVaR model: Instrument z is correlated with the endogenous regressor x and influences the outcome y only indirectly through x, while an unobserved confounder u affects both x and y.
abstract: We study instrumental variable regression (IVaR) under differential privacy constraints. Classical IVaR methods (like two-stage least squares regression) rely on solving moment equations that directly use sensitive covariates and instruments, creating significant risks of privacy leakage and posing challenges in designing algorithms that are both statistically efficient and differentially private. We propose a noisy two-stage gradient descent algorithm that ensures $Ï$-zero-concentrated differential privacy by injecting carefully calibrated noise into the gradient updates. Our analysis establishes finite-sample convergence rates for the proposed method, showing that the algorithm achieves consistency while preserving privacy. In particular, we derive precise bounds quantifying the trade-off among optimization, privacy, and sampling error. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to provide both privacy guarantees and provable convergence rates for instrumental variable regression in linear models. We further validate our theoretical findings with experiments on both synthetic and real datasets, demonstrating that our method offers practical accuracy-privacy trade-offs.
